01 / A little deduction

Minesweeper

Six mines, thirty safe squares. See what the numbers tell you.

0 / 30 safe0 / 6 flagsBoard 1

Choose a covered square.

View saved sessions

How to play

  1. Click a covered square to reveal it. The number counts mines in its eight surrounding squares. Empty areas open together.
  2. Think a square contains a mine? Click “Place flags”, then click that square. Click a flag again to remove it. Switch back to “Reveal squares” to keep playing.
  3. Reveal all 30 safe squares to win. Opening a mine ends the round. Flags are reminders; they do not prove that a square is safe.
  4. “Restart board” repeats the current layout. “Try another board” cycles through three practice layouts.

Each board starts with a safe opening. Some choices may require a guess. All controls work with a mouse or a tap.

02 / Remember the little things

Memory Match

Turn over two cards. Find their partners. Take as long as you like.

0 / 8 pairs0 turnsBest —Deal 1

Choose two cards to look for a pair.

View saved sessions

How to play

  1. Click two different cards to reveal their symbols. A matching pair stays face up.
  2. If they do not match, take a moment to remember them. Click “Turn cards over” before choosing again.
  3. Find all eight pairs. Try to finish in fewer turns; eight turns is a perfect round.
  4. “New deal” cycles through three prepared arrangements. Your best completed round stays visible until you leave or reload this page.

No countdown, no auto-flipping cards, and no typing. The whole game waits for your next click.

03 / Bring a friend

Tic-tac-toe

Two players, one screen. Three in a row settles it.

X wins 0Draws 0O wins 0

X goes first

Player X, choose an empty square.

View saved sessions

How to play

  1. Take turns clicking an empty square. Player X starts the first round, followed by player O.
  2. Make a line of three matching marks horizontally, vertically, or diagonally to win.
  3. If all nine squares fill without a line, the round is a draw.
  4. “New round” clears the board and alternates the starting player. “Reset scores” starts a fresh match with X first.

This is a local two-player game, not a computer opponent. Scores last while this page stays open.

04 / Find a route, not just a number

Connect the Dots

Connect checkpoints 1–5 in order, using every square exactly once.

1 / 25 squaresNext 20 undosPuzzle 1

Start at 1 and choose a neighbouring square.

View saved sessions

How to play

  1. The route starts at checkpoint 1. Click a square immediately above, below, left or right of your current position to extend it.
  2. Pass through checkpoints 2, 3 and 4 in order. Finish at 5 only after visiting all 25 squares.
  3. You cannot revisit or cross your route. Leave enough room to reach the remaining checkpoints.
  4. If you get stuck, click Undo last step or click the previous square on the route. Start again clears the board; Next puzzle changes the layout.

All three puzzles have a solution. There is no countdown or automatic hint showing the next square.

05 / Every click has neighbours

Lights Out

Turn every light off. Each switch also changes its neighbours.

0 lights on0 movesPuzzle 1

Turn all the lights off.

View saved sessions

How to play

  1. Click a square to switch it and its immediate neighbours above, below, left and right.
  2. A bright square is on; a dark square is off. Make the entire board dark.
  3. Clicking the same square twice cancels that change. The order of your switches does not matter.
  4. All three starting patterns are solvable. Restart repeats the pattern; Next puzzle changes it.

Try to use as few moves as possible. There is no timer.

06 / Make room for the next move

Sliding Tiles

One empty space. Eight tiles to put back in order.

0 movesGoal 1–8

Click a tile beside the empty space.

Target: 1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 empty. Raised tiles can move.

View saved sessions

How to play

  1. Click a tile immediately beside the empty square. It slides into that space. Diagonal moves are not allowed.
  2. Put the tiles in numerical order from left to right, with the empty square at the bottom right.
  3. Every starting position is made by legal moves from the solved board, so it is always solvable.
  4. New puzzle starts a different scramble and clears the move counter.

Plan ahead: placing a tile correctly can require moving it away again first.

07 / Read the feedback

Codebreaker

Find the four-colour code in eight guesses.

0 / 8 guessesCode 1

Click each position to cycle: Red, Blue, Gold, Green, Purple, Orange.

Choose four different colours.

Your clues
TryYour codeRight placeWrong place
View saved sessions

How to play

  1. Click each peg to choose a colour, then click Check code. Use four different colours from the six available.
  2. Right place counts colours in their correct position. Wrong place counts correct colours that belong elsewhere. The feedback does not identify which pegs are correct.
  3. Use earlier clues to narrow down the code. You have eight valid guesses. Incomplete or repeated-colour guesses do not use a turn.
  4. New code cycles between three prepared secret codes. The solution is revealed when the round ends.

Every colour also has a letter or name, so you do not need to distinguish colours alone.
